cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul asks the question out loud, then shuts it down right away: "Certainly not!" He follows with, "How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?" So what he's really saying is that sinning more to get more grace makes no sense for people who died to sin.

The reason Paul gives is that they died to sin. It's right there in verse 2: "How can we who died to sin live in it any longer?" Paul doesn't say believers are trying hard to hold back. He says they died to sin. A person who has died isn't going back to the old house.

The answer is walk in newness of life. Paul says, "…we too may walk in newness of life." Christ was raised through the glory of the Father, and Paul says believers may walk in newness of life too. Notice he says walk, friends. That's an everyday, one-foot-in-front-of-the-other kind of word, not a once-a-year kind.

The answer is True. Paul says it with confidence: "For if we have been united with Him like this in His death, we will certainly also be united with Him in His resurrection." Look at that word certainly. Paul isn't saying maybe or we'll see. He's saying it's settled.

The answer is slaves to sin. Verse 6 says, "…that we should no longer be slaves to sin." The old self was crucified with Christ so that "…the body of sin might be rendered powerless…" Paul's point is that believers are no longer slaves to sin.

The answer is False. Paul puts it in two parts: "…He cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him." Christ was raised from the dead, and death doesn't rule Him. That's the kind of fact you can lean your whole weight on, friends.

The answer is once for all. Paul says it just like that: "The death He died, He died to sin once for all…" (Romans 6:10). It's finished, friends. No repeat, no encore. Once for all means the one time was enough.

The answer is righteousness. The contrast is the whole point: "…instruments of wickedness…" on one side, "…instruments of righteousness." on the other. Paul says to present yourselves to God as those brought from death to life. Then the parts of the body go to Him too, as instruments of righteousness. Same hands, new boss.

The answer is grace. Here's the reason Paul gives: "For sin shall not be your master, because you are not under law, but under grace." Grace is where Paul started this whole passage, when he asked about grace increasing. Now he closes on it, friends. Believers live under grace, and sin doesn't get to be their master.
